protocol.legal_basis: This extended practice authority (EPA) has been made under section 232 of Medicines and Poisons Act 2019 (Qld) by the Deputy Director-General, Health Workforce Division, as a delegate of the chief executive, Queensland Health. For the purposes of Schedule 9, Part 1, Division 1 of the Medicines and Poisons (Medicines) Regulation 2021 (Qld) (MPMR) the EPA details the requirements for a pharmacist to be authorised to deal with the medicines (regulated substances) listed as authorised medicines.
protocol.supervision_model: authorised (document terminology: a pharmacist 'may be authorised to deal with the medicines (regulated substances) listed as authorised medicines'; conditions include successfully completed training in accordance with Appendix 1, and for prescribing services the pharmacist's name must appear on the prescriber register maintained by the Department)
protocol.scope_summary: Legal instrument (Extended practice authority – Pharmacists – version 10) made under section 232 of the Medicines and Poisons Act 2019 (Qld) covering four Queensland Community Pharmacy services: Part 1 Urinary Tract Infection Community Pharmacy Service (sell listed medicines without a prescription for acute uncomplicated cystitis in female patients aged 18-65 years); Part 2 Hormonal Contraception Community Pharmacy Service; Part 3 Fluoride Community Pharmacy Service; Part 4 General Health Community Pharmacy Services (multiple indications per Appendix 4). Includes training requirements (Appendix 1), authorised medicine lists (Appendices 2-4) with indications and age restrictions, clinical record and prescription requirements.

diagnosis_pathways.name: Urinary Tract Infection Community Pharmacy Service (Part 1)

steps.description: Confirm pharmacist and service requirements. A pharmacist who is working in a community pharmacy and has successfully completed the Urinary tract infection training in accordance with Appendix 1 may sell a medicine listed in Appendix 2, Column 1 of this EPA. Appendix 1 Part 1 training must include learning objectives on classification and epidemiology of urinary tract infections, anatomy, pathogenesis, assessment and differential diagnosis, treatment and the urinary tract infection community pharmacy service, and must be one (or more) of: a. the training program developed for the Urinary Tract Infection Pharmacy Pilot – Queensland; b. training delivered through a higher education institution accredited by the Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency; or c. training delivered through a Registered Training Organisation accredited by the Australian Skills Quality Authority.

gates.criterion: Pharmacist is working in a community pharmacy and has successfully completed the Urinary tract infection training in accordance with Appendix 1

provenance.section_heading: Part 1 – Urinary Tract Infection Community Pharmacy Service

steps.description: Assessment recorded in the clinical record. The pharmacist must, when selling a medicine under Appendix 2, Column 1 of this EPA, keep a record of the sold medicine in accordance with section 160 of the MPMR; in addition to keeping a clinical record. This clinical record must include relevant patient health history, problems identified, actions taken, details of contact with other healthcare professionals, and the outcomes of any actions taken.

diagnosis_pathways.name: Prescribing and administration services under the EPA (Parts 2, 3 and 4)

steps.description: Confirm pharmacist authorisation for the service. Part 2 (Hormonal Contraception): a pharmacist working in a community pharmacy who has successfully completed the Hormonal contraception training in accordance with Appendix 1; the pharmacist's name must appear on the prescriber register maintained by the Department for the hormonal contraception community pharmacy service. Part 3 (Fluoride): a pharmacist who has successfully completed training in the application of topical fluoride varnish (Fluoride training) in accordance with Appendix 1 may administer a Schedule 4 medicine that is fluoride in a topical preparation for human use. Part 4 (General Health): a pharmacist who has successfully completed the General health services training in accordance with Appendix 1; the pharmacist's name must appear on the prescriber register maintained by the Department for general health community pharmacy services. Appendix 1 Part 4 training must be a tertiary-level study program equivalent to Australian Qualifications Framework Level 8 comprising an Australian Pharmacy Council accredited prescribing training program and a clinical skills training program.

gates.criterion: Pharmacist has successfully completed the training required for the service in accordance with Appendix 1
Pharmacist's name appears on the prescriber register maintained by the Department (Parts 2 and 4)

provenance.section_heading: Part 2 – Hormonal Contraception Community Pharmacy Service

steps.description: Individualised clinical assessment and clinical record (Part 2 clause 2.4, page 2; Part 4 clause 4.4, page 3). When prescribing the medicine, the pharmacist must make an individualised clinical assessment of the patient's health needs and suitability for the prescribed treatment; and keep a clinical record of the consultation with the patient that includes: a. Relevant patient history; b. An assessment of the requirement for the prescribed medicine (Part 2: 'of the requirement for the prescribed medicine'; Part 4: 'of the condition that requires the prescribed medicine'); and c. The management plan for treating the patient's condition including: i. The name of the medicine prescribed; ii. The strength of the medicine prescribed; iii. The formulation of the medicine prescribed; iv. The instructions for use of the medicine prescribed; v. The amount of the medicine prescribed. (Part 2 additionally requires an individualised clinical assessment of the patient's contraceptive and sexual health needs and suitability for hormonal contraception and management.)

provenance.section_heading: Part 2 – Hormonal Contraception Community Pharmacy Service

steps.description: Confirm indication and age/restriction eligibility. Part 2: a female patient aged 16 years or older, subject to the restrictions for the medicine stated opposite in Appendix 3, Column 2 (if any) - combined hormonal contraception (combined oral contraceptives (COCs) and the contraceptive vaginal ring) excluding preparations containing 50 micrograms or more of ethinylestradiol, or preparations containing mestranol; progesterone-only contraceptive pill and depot medroxyprogesterone (injection) have no restriction printed. Part 4: the indication must be the indication listed in Appendix 4, Column 2 (e.g. acute exacerbations of mild plaque psoriasis - aged 16 years or over; acute nausea and vomiting associated with gastroenteritis - aged 18 years or over; acute minor wound management - aged 5 years or over; acute otitis externa and acute otitis media - aged 2 years or over; allergic and nonallergic rhinitis - no age printed, excluding ocular medicines containing ketorolac or corticosteroids; gastro-oesophageal reflux and gastro-oesophageal reflux disease - aged 18 years to 55 years; impetigo - aged 1 year or over; management for the overweight and obesity - aged 18 years or over, excluding liraglutide, semaglutide and naltrexone + bupropion; mild to moderate acne - aged 12 years or over; mild to moderate atopic dermatitis - aged 6 months or over; mild, acute, musculoskeletal pain - aged 18 years or over; shingles pain - aged 18 years or over; nicotine dependence - aged 18 years or over, excluding nortriptyline and nicotine vaping products; acute mountain sickness - aged 8 years or over; travellers' diarhoea - aged 2 years or over; malaria prophylaxis or standby emergency treatment of uncomplicated malaria - aged 8 years or over), subject to the restrictions stated opposite in Appendix 4, Column 3.

gates.criterion: Indication is the indication listed in Appendix 4, Column 2 (or Appendix 3 for hormonal contraception) and the patient meets the restriction stated in Column 3

steps.description: Prescribe. When prescribing a medicine, the pharmacist must make a written prescription that is compliant with Chapter 4, Part 6, Division 3 of the MPMR (Parts 2 and 4). The pharmacist must take all reasonable steps to prescribe the medicine in accordance with the current online version of the section/s of the Therapeutic Guidelines specified within Appendix 4, Column 1 (Part 4) or titled 'Sexual and Reproductive Health: Contraception' (Part 2). Quantity limit: the pharmacist must not prescribe, in one prescription, greater than 12 months' supply of a medicine listed in Appendix 3 or Appendix 4 of this EPA. Part 3 fluoride: administration of a Schedule 4 medicine that is fluoride in a topical preparation for human use following completion of Fluoride training.

gates.criterion: Written prescription is compliant with Chapter 4, Part 6, Division 3 of the MPMR
Prescription does not exceed 12 months' supply of a medicine listed in Appendix 3 or Appendix 4

provenance.section_heading: Part 4 – General Health Community Pharmacy Services

steps.description: Record keeping. Keep the clinical record of the consultation as required by clauses 2.4 (Part 2) and 4.4 (Part 4), including relevant patient history, assessment, and the management plan details (medicine name, strength, formulation, instructions for use, amount).

provenance.section_heading: Part 4 – General Health Community Pharmacy Services

steps.description: Part 3 fluoride administration conditions. A pharmacist who is working in a community pharmacy and has successfully completed training in the application of topical fluoride varnish (Fluoride training) in accordance with Appendix 1 may administer a Schedule 4 medicine that is fluoride in a topical preparation for human use. Fluoride training must include: a. assessing patient suitability for topical fluoride varnish application, including identification of clinical indicators, risk factors, and contraindications; b. understanding the mechanism of action of topical fluoride in caries prevention; c. recognising and managing potential safety risks associated with topical fluoride use; d. providing patient advice on oral hygiene practices and preventive dental care.

gates.criterion: Patient suitability for topical fluoride varnish application assessed (clinical indicators, risk factors, contraindications)

open_questions.observed: Page 6 lists Cefalexin, Fosfomycin, Nitrofurantoin and Trimethoprim under 'Regulated substance' with the 'Restrictions/Conditions' column showing no entries for any of the four medicines. Clause 1.1(a) nevertheless refers to 'the restrictions for the medicine stated opposite in Appendix 2, Column 2 (if any)'.

open_questions.topic: Appendix 3 restrictions printed for only one of three rows
open_questions.observed: Only the combined hormonal contraception row carries a restriction ('Excluding preparations containing 50 micrograms or more of ethinylestradiol, or preparations containing mestranol.'); the progesterone-only contraceptive pill and depot medroxyprogesterone (injection) rows show no restriction content.
open_questions.why_unclear: Cannot tell whether no restrictions apply or extraction lost content.

open_questions.topic: Lidocaine row in Appendix 4 has no indication or restriction content
open_questions.observed: Page 7 prints the row 'Lidocaine preparations of 1% or less in accordance with ... "Pain and analgesia: Drugs used for pain: Local anaesthetics for acute pain management".' with no text in the Indication or Restrictions/Conditions columns in the extraction; it sits between the 'Acute minor wound management' row (aged 5 years or over) and the 'Acute otitis externa' row (aged 2 years or over).
open_questions.why_unclear: Table row is ambiguous/misaligned in the text extraction; the indication and age restriction for lidocaine cannot be attributed with confidence.

open_questions.topic: Combinatorics of criteria not stated by the document
open_questions.observed: The EPA states AND-combinatorics within each clause ('subject to ... a. ... and b. ...'; clause 4.1 'a. for the indication ... and b. subject to the restrictions ... and c. ...'), but does not state how the four Parts (1-4) or the Appendix 4 rows combine. Per-Part all_of groups and per-row groups were formed from the document structure (each Appendix 4 row's group includes the Part 4 conditions INC-14 to INC-18 plus the row itself). Exclusion groups were defaulted to all_of with confidence 'unclear' per spec because the document states no combinatorics for the prohibitions (each prohibition is specific to its own medicine/indication/service).
open_questions.why_unclear: Document does not state combinatorics across Parts, rows or exclusions; recorded here as required by the spec.

open_questions.topic: No referral or escalation instruction when service criteria are not met
open_questions.observed: The EPA contains no referral criteria, red-flag clinical triggers or escalation instructions; where a patient does not meet a service criterion (e.g. female aged between 18 and 65 years for acute uncomplicated cystitis), the document only withholds the authority to supply under the EPA.
open_questions.why_unclear: Gates use on_fail STOP as the boundary of the authority; the document does not say to refer, escalate or how to handle the patient otherwise.

open_questions.observed: No strengths, doses, routes, frequencies or durations are printed for any medicine; supply/prescribing must follow named current online Therapeutic Guidelines sections ('Antibiotic: Urinary tract infections in adults: Acute cystitis in adults'; 'Sexual and Reproductive Health: Contraception'; specified Appendix 4 sections).
open_questions.why_unclear: Treatment rows have empty dose/strength/frequency fields because the instrument does not print them; first_line is set false for all treatments because no medicine ranking/first-line designation is printed.

open_questions.observed: Age bounds differ per service: UTI 'aged between 18 and 65 years' (page 1); hormonal contraception 'aged 16 years or older' (page 2); Appendix 4 rows: 16 years or over (psoriasis), 18 years or over (antiemetic, weight, musculoskeletal pain, shingles, nicotine dependence), 5 years or over (minor wound), 2 years or over (otitis externa, otitis media, travellers' diarhoea), 18 years to 55 years (gastro-oesophageal reflux), 1 year or over (impetigo), 12 years or over (acne), 6 months or over (atopic dermatitis), 8 years or over (acute mountain sickness, malaria); rhinitis row prints no age restriction. age_bounds therefore records the lowest printed minimum (6 months) and no overall maximum.
open_questions.why_unclear: No single overall age range is stated for the instrument as a whole.

open_questions.observed: The EPA requires records of sold medicines under section 160 of the MPMR plus clinical records, and prescriber register maintenance by the Department, but prints no notifiable-condition, GP-notification or AIR requirements. The document has no reference list.
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec: notifiable.required is null if the document is silent; references array is empty because none are printed.
